digest.top_line: Consolidative TRT + atezolizumab maintenance in ES-SCLC: mOS 6.7 vs 13.4 mo (HR 1.55), halted for fatal toxicity (19.4% vs 3.0%).
digest.tldr: One thoracic randomised phase 2 carries the day, and it is a stop sign: adding 30 Gy/10 fx consolidative TRT to atezolizumab maintenance in ES-SCLC halved mOS and quadrupled fatal AEs, with TRT (not atezolizumab) tracking AE risk. Echoes PACIFIC-2 and CheckMate-73L on RT plus checkpoint blockade. Halted at 68 of 104 pts, so efficacy is descriptive.

sites.intro: Consolidative thoracic RT layered onto checkpoint maintenance in ES-SCLC: toxicity, not efficacy, ended the trial.

studies.name: Consolidative TRT + Atezolizumab Maintenance in ES-SCLC
studies.tldr: mOS 6.7 vs 13.4 mo (HR 1.55, P = .34) adding consolidative TRT to atezolizumab maintenance; halted for fatal toxicity.
details: 🔍 Randomised phase 2, 20 sites in Germany and Austria, N=68 (34 per arm), open-label
🔍 TRT 30 Gy in 10 fx to postinduction thoracic primary plus nodal metastases
📊 ALC below normal by cycle 2 in 91.7% of arm A vs 13.6% (P < .001)
📐 TRT tracked with AE risk (HR 2.47, 1.15-5.32, P = .01), atezolizumab exposure did not (HR 0.57, P = .06)
🔗 Arm B mOS 13.4 mo and 1-y OS 56.6% exceed the IMpower133 atezolizumab arm (12.3 mo, 51.7%)
🔗 Echoes PACIFIC-2 and CheckMate-73L: more fatal toxicity when thoracic RT meets checkpoint blockade
⚠️ Halted at 68 of 104 planned pts; power drastically reduced, so the efficacy read is descriptive

verdict.rationale: Randomised, prespecified safety endpoints; SAE and fatal-AE differences significant despite the early halt. OS underpowered and descriptive, but the toxicity signal contests consolidative TRT in the IO era.
verdict.audience: ES-SCLC, at least SD after carboplatin-etoposide-atezolizumab induction

studies.significance: Baseline DLCO SB separated the fatal cases (45.3 vs 56.7, P = .04), the only patient-level signal found, since no dosimetric parameter and no concurrent vs sequential timing tracked with SAEs. Dose was modest (30 Gy/10 fx to postinduction volumes), so the harm is not a dose-escalation artefact.
studies.monday_clinic: In unselected ES-SCLC with at least stable disease after carboplatin-etoposide-atezolizumab induction, this questions adding consolidative TRT during maintenance outside a trial; it does not address TRT integrated with induction chemoimmunotherapy or delivered without concurrent PD-L1 blockade.

primary_endpoint.name: Overall survival
primary_endpoint.stat_detail: HR 1.55 (95% CI 0.90-2.69), P = .34; primary end point not met

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Multicenter open-label phase 2 RCT (TREASURE, AIO-TRK-0320), randomised 1:1 at 20 sites in Germany and Austria, accruing September 2020 to August 2022 with follow-up to September 2024. Powered for a **20% absolute gain in 12-month survival (72% vs 52%, HR 0.57)**, needing 66 events and 104 randomised pts.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: ES-SCLC with **at least stable disease** after induction carboplatin, etoposide and atezolizumab; 96 assessed, 68 randomised (71%). Stratified by brain metastases, induction response and prophylactic cranial irradiation. Baseline ECOG, comorbidity, pulmonary function and thoracic tumour burden were balanced between arms.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **30 Gy in 10 fractions**, target volume delineated on the postinduction thoracic primary and nodal metastases. Doses and volumes sat within or below typical clinical ranges and below established OAR thresholds. Concurrent vs sequential delivery relative to atezolizumab was **not** associated with AE occurrence.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary: OS** from randomisation to death from any cause. Secondary: PFS plus frequency and severity of AEs and SAEs. Stratified log-rank and multivariable Cox in ITT, with per-protocol and fatal-AE-excluded sensitivity sets.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: A sensitivity analysis excluding fatal AEs gave consistent OS, so the arm A deficit is **not solely driven by those deaths**. A post hoc update after 19 further months of follow-up was unchanged.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: SAEs were predominantly infections (urinary, pulmonary) and respiratory disorders, with dysphagia, esophagitis, fever and skin events also more frequent in arm A. The prespecified pneumonitis gate was passed (1 grade 3 or higher event among the first 23 arm A pts); the excess sat in **non-pneumonitis fatal SAEs**. Grade 3 or higher trAEs in arm A (**26%**) exceed benchmarks for atezolizumab alone and for consolidative TRT without immunotherapy.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents unselected ES-SCLC pts with at least stable disease after chemoimmunotherapy induction, receiving consolidative TRT during atezolizumab maintenance. Does not represent limited-stage SCLC, TRT integrated with induction chemoimmunotherapy, or pts selected by baseline pulmonary function.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Causal attribution was contested: treating investigators judged 4 arm A deaths unrelated, the SMC reclassified 3 as possibly or probably related. Open-label, and no clinical or dosimetric parameter predicted SAEs, so no criterion emerges for selecting pts who might still receive TRT safely.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: PFS was superimposable while OS diverged, pointing to treatment-related toxic effects rather than accelerated progression as the driver. OS curves crossed at roughly 24 months, but few pts remained at risk, so that late reversal carries little weight.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Baseline DLCO SB separated the fatal cases (45.3 vs 56.7, P = .04), the only patient-level signal, while dose, volume and concurrent vs sequential timing did not track with SAEs. At 30 Gy in 10 fx to postinduction volumes, this harm is not a dose-escalation artefact.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: The maintenance-only arm reached mOS 13.4 mo and 1-y OS 56.6%, above the IMpower133 atezolizumab arm (12.3 mo, 51.7%), so the comparator was not underperforming. Lymphopenia persisted to cycle 4 (69.2% vs 8.3% below normal), which reframes infection surveillance in any irradiated pt on maintenance.

open_questions: Can baseline DLCO or lymphocyte-sparing planning select pts who tolerate consolidative TRT?
Does deferring TRT until after maintenance avoid the lymphodepletion-infection cascade?

papers.title: Consolidative Thoracic Radiotherapy With Atezolizumab Maintenance in Extensive-Stage Small Cell Lung Cancer
papers.abstract: Importance Chemoimmunotherapy followed by immunotherapy maintenance is the standard first-line treatment for extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC), yet data regarding efficacy and safety of consolidative thoracic radiotherapy (TRT) are lacking. Objective To determine whether combining consolidative TRT with immunotherapy maintenance in ES-SCLC is safe and improves patients’ overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). Design, Settings, and Participants This was a multicenter open-label phase 2 randomized clinical trial recruiting patients from September 2020 to August 2022 in Germany and Austria, with the last follow-up visit in September 2024. Eligible patients had ES-SCLC with at least stable disease after induction chemoimmunotherapy (carboplatin−etoposide−atezolizumab). Although the database was locked in April 2025, a post hoc survival update was performed in April 2026. Data were analyzed from April 2025 to April 2026. Interventions Randomized (1:1) to either atezolizumab maintenance combined with consolidative TRT (30 Gy in 10 fractions) (arm A) or atezolizumab maintenance alone (arm B). Main Outcome and Measure OS (time from randomization to death due to any cause). Results Of 96 patients assessed for eligibility, 68 patients were randomized; recruitment was prematurely terminated due to safety concerns. Median OS in the combination arm was numerically shorter compared to atezolizumab only (6.7 months [95% CI, 5.1-9.0] vs 13.4 months [95% CI, 10.7-17.5]; HR, 1.55 [95% CI, 0.90-2.69]; P = .34), while median PFS was similar (2.4 months [95% CI, 1.3-3.9] vs 2.6 months [95% CI, 1.2-3.9]; HR, 0.92 [95% CI, 0.54-1.55]; P = .85). TRT plus atezolizumab was accompanied by higher frequency of severe adverse events (SAEs) (19 patients [61.3%] vs 6 patients [18.2%]; P &amp;lt; .001) and fatal outcomes (6 patients [19.4%] vs 1 patient [3.0%]; P = .04). Safety analysis revealed predominance of infection and respiratory disorder−related SAEs, possibly facilitated by a depletion of lymphocytes observed specifically in patients after TRT, and by a lower single breath diffuse capacity of the lungs for carbon monoxide in patients with fatal AEs in arm A. No further risk factors were identified, given that baseline characteristics were well balanced between both arms and between patients with and without SAEs, including fatal SAEs. Conclusions and Relevance In this randomized clinical trial, TRT combined with immunotherapy increased toxic effects in unselected patients with ES-SCLC without survival benefit, presumably due to radiation-induced lymphocyte depletion facilitating infections. Cautious patient selection and further investigation to identify those who may benefit without undue risk are required. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04462276
